title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Minor and inessential: Grothendieck crossed out 'une unique' completion. The completion with smooth boundary points is in fact unique up to unique isomorphism: near I it is the unique smooth completion of the smooth locus, and X̂ is obtained by glueing. Uniqueness could have been asserted.
Condition (a) is slightly redundant: a separated, finite-type, 1-dimensional scheme is automatically quasi-projective.
Finite type, separatedness and reducedness are implicit rather than stated. Reducedness follows from the local condition (b).

ideas.what: Open nodal curves ('courbes standard'): quasi-projective curves with only smooth points and ordinary double points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969; Knudsen 1983 for the pointed version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses M_{g,ν} and their boundary informally, but not this definition

ideas.what: Equivalence between an open nodal curve X and a pair (X̂, I): a proper nodal curve with a finite set of smooth marked points, via the unique smooth-at-infinity completion
ideas.modern_name: pointed nodal curve / punctured curve correspondence

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine foundational definition of punctured nodal curves, standard since Deligne–Mumford and Knudsen. The only slightly characteristic touch is taking open curves as the primary objects, in view of the later Teichmüller and fundamental-groupoid study, but this is not new.
transcription_corrections: Line 'est [-une-] schéma': the struck-out word looks longer than 'une', possibly 'une courbe' or a false start. It is immaterial.
Transcription otherwise matches the image, including the inserted phrases 'toute composante irréd. est' and 'X̂ soit un schéma propre, que', and the struck-out 'une unique'.
